rows.title: Minimal fix/mix nucleus
rows.boundary: The explicit recursive Interaction calculus has a total finite observer, an unbounded inductive operational semantics, soundness/completeness, stable observations, divergence correspondence and related-carrier transfer. It supports heterogeneous inherited carriers and delayed values. Arbitrary Scheme programs are outside the stated calculus. Call-by-need caches carry evaluation proofs indexed by the exact program; completed source errors are shared. Active cycles are separate runtime diagnostics. Mutable writes reset the cache and advance the generation. Every finite operational value/error derivation completes at some machine budget from any sound warm cache. Completed results and cycles are stable under increasing budgets; reported cycles prove divergence. Certified instance and mutable reads retain the exact request/snapshot divergence proof. Exhaustion alone remains inconclusive. Actual safe C3 methods now accept parameters and preserve final-self and delayed inherited calls, including argument forwarding. The existing recursive machine shares the complete method name/argument request, reports parameterized cycles with divergence proofs, and distinguishes changing-argument recursion from a repeated request. Dynamic argument equality is computable and kernel justified. Existing value-only object observations are preserved at every depth by the request reindexing theorem. The declared Interaction compiler now executes through the existing unsafe sharedFix/instantiate constructor, records native demand traces, and uses a total safe checker to reconstruct exact-program evaluation proofs and compare reported values/errors. Shared demand executions and safe Evaluates derivations are equivalent; bounded recordings agree at every source depth, and every finite derivation has an admitted trace. A sequential private-cell operational model proves current-body identity, installation before forcing and exactly one constructor start for every ready heap. Checked native C3 field/method reads transfer to existing plan and source graph derivations. These native closures share construction rather than request results. Native IO.Ref/Thunk/compiler/concurrency behavior and arbitrary unsafe callbacks remain runtime boundaries; no unchecked unsafe fixed-point equation is assumed.
